hero.headline: Three Port St. Lucie police officers placed on leave during campaign sign investigations
hero.teaser: The Port St. Lucie Police Department placed Detective Sgt. Sean Smith, Officer Jason Vega, and Detective Sgt. on paid administrative leave as the Florida Department of Law Enforcement takes over a criminal investigation into two incidents involving political campaign signs near SW Airoso Boulevard.
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie Police Department placed three officers on paid administrative leave effective August 13 as part of investigations into two incidents involving political campaign signs near SW Airoso Boulevard last week. The officers placed on leave are Detective Sgt. Sean Smith, Officer Jason Vega, and Detective Sgt. Chief Leo Niemczyk reviewed the initial facts and timeline surrounding the incidents before requesting assistance from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement to ensure the investigation remains fair, impartial, and unbiased.

FDLE has agreed to take over the criminal investigation into the campaign sign incidents. The department stated the criminal investigation must be completed before the internal administrative investigation begins to ensure both processes are conducted independently and appropriately. Once the criminal investigation concludes, the internal administrative investigation will proceed in accordance with established procedures, applicable law, and the Florida Law Enforcement Officers' Bill of Rights. The Port St. Lucie Police Department stated it will not provide additional information or comment on matters being handled by FDLE.

cards.headline: Homeowner shoots, kills man who attacked him at St. Lucie County mobile home park; stand your ground case under review
cards.teaser: A 37-year-old man died Wednesday night after a 22-year-old homeowner shot him inside a residence at Seminole Mobile Home Park in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue following a physica
cards.body:
A 37-year-old man died Wednesday night after a 22-year-old homeowner shot him inside a residence at Seminole Mobile Home Park in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue following a physical attack that stemmed from an ongoing dispute between the two men. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the men had exchanged threatening text messages and verbal arguments before the shooting occurred at 9:11 p.m. The man who was killed knocked on the door, was let inside, then immediately pushed the homeowner and punched him twice in the midsection. The homeowner backed away, pulled out a 9 mm semi-automatic pistol, and shot the man once in the chest.

The man who was shot was taken to a local hospital, where he died from his injuries. The homeowner's sister and girlfriend were inside the home at the time and gave statements that corroborated his account of the incident. Investigators executed a search warrant at the residence and recovered the handgun. The sheriff said the suspect had a criminal history including drug-related charges, resisting officer charges, domestic violence-related charges, and three felony convictions.

No charges have been filed against the homeowner. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is working with the State Attorney's Office to determine whether the shooting falls under Florida's stand your ground self-defense law. Del Toro said investigators worked nine hours at the scene, which was cleared shortly after 6 a.m. Thursday. The name of the man who was killed has not been released.

Investigators described the shooting as an isolated incident and said there is no immediate threat to the surrounding community. Del Toro urged anyone who receives threats and believes a situation could escalate to contact law enforcement before violence occurs. The sheriff's office is asking anyone with information about the shooting to call 772-462-3230 or submit anonymous tips through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-TIPS.

cards.headline: 16-year-old girl dies after falling through roof of abandoned Sebastian building
cards.teaser: A 16-year-old girl died after falling approximately 29 feet through a hole in the roof of an abandoned four-story building in Sebastian on Saturday night. Deputies said the group had been trespassing on the property.
cards.body:
A 16-year-old girl died after she fell through a hole in the roof of an abandoned four-story building last Saturday in Sebastian, deputies said. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office responded to 9846 Riverside Preserve Drive in Sebastian at about 10:35 p.m. after receiving a 911 call reporting that the girl had fallen from a concrete structure and was critically injured. Deputies arrived and found a group of minors along with the critically injured teen on the second floor of the abandoned building.

The investigation determined the group had been trespassing on the property and was on the roof when the teen fell through a hole in the roof, dropping approximately 29 feet to the floor below, the sheriff's office said. One of the minors in the group knew CPR and immediately began life-saving measures. The 16-year-old was flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where she died from her injuries a short time later.

Detectives are actively investigating the teen's death, but said at this time, all evidence indicates this was an accident. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office extends its deepest sympathies to the family during this difficult time. We also want to remind the public, especially parents and teens, of the serious dangers posed by climbing on abandoned structures, and the legal consequences of trespassing on privately owned property, the sheriff's office said.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds leads Florida Republican gubernatorial primary with 49% as Aug. 18 vote nears
cards.teaser: Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary stands at a decisive tilt five days before the Aug. 18 election, with U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds holding a commanding lead while Democrats a
cards.body:
Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary stands at a decisive tilt five days before the Aug. 18 election, with U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds holding a commanding lead while Democrats appear near settling their nomination. A James Madison Institute survey released in August placed Donalds at 49 percent among likely Republican primary voters, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 18 percent, former House Speaker Paul Renner at 8 percent and investor James Fishback at 4 percent. Twenty-one percent remained undecided.

Donalds, who secured President Donald Trump's endorsement, centered his closing message on affordability and promised to lower Florida property insurance costs through changes to the state's Catastrophe Fund, reinsurance system and home hardening programs. He called the property tax amendment headed to voters only a first step and argued that faster permitting could reduce housing and construction costs. Donalds told reporters he feels confident about his position but acknowledged the outcome remains in voters' hands.

Collins escalated his attacks in a lengthy virtual news conference, casting himself as a day-one ready Florida executive and Donalds as a Washington celebrity disconnected from working families. Collins proposed tighter insurance oversight, faster claims and storm permitting, expanded home hardening and the eventual elimination of property taxes on homesteaded homes. He called the Republican contest a two-person race and urged Renner, Fishback and other candidates without viable paths to rally behind him, though recent public polling consistently shows Donalds leading by wide margins. Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025 but has not endorsed anyone in the race to succeed him.

On the Democratic side, former Republican congressman David Jolly held 47 percent in the latest JMI survey, with no other Democratic candidate topping 5 percent. His running mate Gwen Graham cast her ballot at Florida A&M University and described the ticket as centrist and moderate, with an agenda focused on housing affordability, education and healthcare access. Florida had nearly 3.33 million voters registered with no party affiliation as of July 31, while Republicans held a registration advantage of more than 1.5 million over Democrats. The latest JMI survey showed Donalds leading Jolly 45 to 38 percent in a potential general election matchup. The primary is Aug. 18, and the general election is Nov. 3.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is feeling the pressure after 36 Border Collies were rescued from a hoarding case in Palm City this week. Sarah Fisher with the Humane Society said the latest case is the worst animal neglect she has ever seen. Fisher told CBS12 News that teams at the Humane Society are overwhelmed by the amount of care and rehabilitation the Border Collies will need, but are prepared to provide the dogs with the medical care, attention and support they desperately need.

Fisher said it will be some time before the dogs are ready for adoption. Once they are ready to find their forever homes, the Humane Society plans to identify families with experience caring for Border Collies. The organization will also look for families who have plenty of patience, because the dogs will need extensive socialization, training and time to adjust to their new surroundings.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police arrest driver in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old in crosswalk
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police have arrested Demetris Johnson, 34, in connection with a hit-and-run crash at North 25th Street and Avenue M that seriously injured a 7-year-old child crossing in a marked crosswalk.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police arrested 34-year-old Demetris Johnson on Wednesday, 11 days after a hit-and-run crash left an 8-year-old girl with a fractured femur. The crash happened at 8:55 p.m. on Saturday, August 1, at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M when a Mercedes-Benz making a left turn struck the girl as she and her brother were crossing the street in a marked crosswalk. Surveillance cameras from a nearby business captured Johnson exiting the vehicle to check on the girl before getting back into the car and driving away.

Johnson was located and arrested at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and faces charges of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injuries and driving while his license was suspended. He refused to speak with investigators. The girl's mother, Lawrunda Robinson, said her daughter is using a wheelchair and will need a month in a cast before beginning physical therapy to learn to walk again. Johnson is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail.

cards.headline: Indian River County deputies talk wanted man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
cards.teaser: Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. De
cards.body:
Deputies in Indian River County safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning. The incident began around 1 a.m. when deputies responded to a call from Port St. Lucie police about a man wanted for burglary. The man had reportedly called his mother and told her he wanted to kill himself.

Body camera footage showed the man sitting on a platform over the bridge railing, his feet dangling in the air. Traffic Deputy Edouard Gast, a member of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team, worked to establish a connection with the man. At one point, the man appeared ready to jump.

The sheriff's office marine unit and fire rescue crews were stationed in the water below as a safety precaution. After two hours of negotiation, the man climbed back to the top of the bridge and shook the negotiator's hand. The man was taken into custody without incident.

hero.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
hero.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is feeling the pressure after 36 Border Collies were rescued from a hoarding case in Palm City this week. Sarah Fisher with the Humane Society said the latest case is the worst animal neglect she has ever seen. Fisher told CBS12 News that teams at the Humane Society are overwhelmed by the amount of care and rehabilitation the Border Collies will need, but are prepared to provide the dogs with the medical care, attention and support they desperately need.

Fisher said it will be some time before the dogs are ready for adoption. Once they are ready to find their forever homes, the Humane Society plans to identify families with experience caring for Border Collies. The organization will also look for families who have plenty of patience, because the dogs will need extensive socialization, training and time to adjust to their new surroundings.

hero.headline: Three Port St. Lucie police officers placed on leave during campaign sign investigations
hero.teaser: The Port St. Lucie Police Department placed Detective Sgt. Sean Smith, Officer Jason Vega, and Detective Sgt. on paid administrative leave as the Florida Department of Law Enforcement takes over a criminal investigation into two incidents involving political campaign signs near SW Airoso Boulevard.
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie Police Department placed three officers on paid administrative leave effective August 13 as part of investigations into two incidents involving political campaign signs near SW Airoso Boulevard last week. The officers placed on leave are Detective Sgt. Sean Smith, Officer Jason Vega, and Detective Sgt. Chief Leo Niemczyk reviewed the initial facts and timeline surrounding the incidents before requesting assistance from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement to ensure the investigation remains fair, impartial, and unbiased.

FDLE has agreed to take over the criminal investigation into the campaign sign incidents. The department stated the criminal investigation must be completed before the internal administrative investigation begins to ensure both processes are conducted independently and appropriately. Once the criminal investigation concludes, the internal administrative investigation will proceed in accordance with established procedures, applicable law, and the Florida Law Enforcement Officers' Bill of Rights. The Port St. Lucie Police Department stated it will not provide additional information or comment on matters being handled by FDLE.

cards.headline: Homeowner shoots, kills man who attacked him at St. Lucie County mobile home park; stand your ground case under review
cards.teaser: A 37-year-old man died Wednesday night after a 22-year-old homeowner shot him inside a residence at Seminole Mobile Home Park in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue following a physica
cards.body:
A 37-year-old man died Wednesday night after a 22-year-old homeowner shot him inside a residence at Seminole Mobile Home Park in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue following a physical attack that stemmed from an ongoing dispute between the two men. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the men had exchanged threatening text messages and verbal arguments before the shooting occurred at 9:11 p.m. The man who was killed knocked on the door, was let inside, then immediately pushed the homeowner and punched him twice in the midsection. The homeowner backed away, pulled out a 9 mm semi-automatic pistol, and shot the man once in the chest.

The man who was shot was taken to a local hospital, where he died from his injuries. The homeowner's sister and girlfriend were inside the home at the time and gave statements that corroborated his account of the incident. Investigators executed a search warrant at the residence and recovered the handgun. The sheriff said the suspect had a criminal history including drug-related charges, resisting officer charges, domestic violence-related charges, and three felony convictions.

No charges have been filed against the homeowner. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is working with the State Attorney's Office to determine whether the shooting falls under Florida's stand your ground self-defense law. Del Toro said investigators worked nine hours at the scene, which was cleared shortly after 6 a.m. Thursday. The name of the man who was killed has not been released.

Investigators described the shooting as an isolated incident and said there is no immediate threat to the surrounding community. Del Toro urged anyone who receives threats and believes a situation could escalate to contact law enforcement before violence occurs. The sheriff's office is asking anyone with information about the shooting to call 772-462-3230 or submit anonymous tips through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-TIPS.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police arrest driver in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old in crosswalk
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police have arrested Demetris Johnson, 34, in connection with a hit-and-run crash at North 25th Street and Avenue M that seriously injured a 7-year-old child crossing in a marked crosswalk.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police arrested 34-year-old Demetris Johnson on Wednesday, 11 days after a hit-and-run crash left an 8-year-old girl with a fractured femur. The crash happened at 8:55 p.m. on Saturday, August 1, at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M when a Mercedes-Benz making a left turn struck the girl as she and her brother were crossing the street in a marked crosswalk. Surveillance cameras from a nearby business captured Johnson exiting the vehicle to check on the girl before getting back into the car and driving away.

Johnson was located and arrested at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and faces charges of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injuries and driving while his license was suspended. He refused to speak with investigators. The girl's mother, Lawrunda Robinson, said her daughter is using a wheelchair and will need a month in a cast before beginning physical therapy to learn to walk again. Johnson is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail.

hero.headline: Indian River County deputies talk wanted man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
hero.teaser: Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. De
hero.body:
Deputies in Indian River County safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning. The incident began around 1 a.m. when deputies responded to a call from Port St. Lucie police about a man wanted for burglary. The man had reportedly called his mother and told her he wanted to kill himself.

Body camera footage showed the man sitting on a platform over the bridge railing, his feet dangling in the air. Traffic Deputy Edouard Gast, a member of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team, worked to establish a connection with the man. At one point, the man appeared ready to jump.

The sheriff's office marine unit and fire rescue crews were stationed in the water below as a safety precaution. After two hours of negotiation, the man climbed back to the top of the bridge and shook the negotiator's hand. The man was taken into custody without incident.
